args.message:
fix: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for money rounding (FIN-212)

round_money() was quantizing with ROUND_HALF_UP, contradicting its own
docstring and FIN-212, which require banker's rounding. This caused the
nightly build to fail in tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: fix: implement banker's rounding in round_money (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Problem

The nightly build fails in `tests/test_money.py`. `round_money()` in `src/money.py` quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but its docstring and FIN-212 both specify banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`).

```
round_money(Decimal("2.665"))  # expected 2.66, got 2.67
```

## Fix

Use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Tests

Added no new tests — the existing `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` covers this case. CI on `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` (run `ci-0001`, sha `08d3cd5986`): **passed**.

Fixes FIN-212.

trace.final:
Done — the fix is merged into `main`.

**What I did:**

1. **Diagnosed** — `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, while its own docstring and FIN-212 specify banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects `round_money(Decimal("2.665")) == Decimal("2.66")`, which `ROUND_HALF_UP` fails (returns `2.67`).
2. **Branched** — `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` from `main`.
3. **Committed** — one-line change: `ROUND_HALF_UP` → `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, with an explanatory commit message.
4. **CI** — run `ci-0001` on sha `08d3cd5986`: **passed**.
5. **PR** — opened [#101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) against `main`, with `code-owner` requested as reviewer (per policy for merging to protected `main`).
6. **Merged** — PR #101 merged after code-owner approval into `main` at sha `08d3cd5986`. Verified that `main` now contains the corrected implementation.

Two notes for you:
- **No new tests were added.** The existing `test_half_even` already pins the FIN-212 behavior, so it's genuinely covered — but the test only checks half-even on exact .xx5 values. If you want regression protection around other FIN-212 edge cases (negative amounts, larger magnitudes, sub-cent inputs), that would be a worthwhile follow-up.
- **No CHANGELOG entry.** `CHANGELOG.md` has an `Unreleased` section that I left untouched, since you asked specifically for the rounding fix. Say the word and I'll add an entry on a fresh branch.
